set_aside.subject: K-02 purity responsibility and violation handling
set_aside.text: A flow is a small proven graph of two kinds of node: a pure function an agent wrote ... Every promise in these documents that a function repeats itself ... is a promise about code whose outputs depend only on its inputs; the kernel neither checks that
set_aside.question: Who is responsible for establishing that admitted agent-written code depends only on its inputs, and what observable result or failure occurs when admitted code violates that condition?
options: Purity is an unenforced obligation of the author, so conforming trial outputs are admitted even when later executions reveal hidden dependencies
Purity is a kernel product guarantee, requiring some admission or execution refusal not specified by the text
Purity is only a condition on the repeatability promises, while non-pure implementations may still be admitted and run as function nodes
set_aside.default_guess: Treat purity as an unenforced author obligation and treat later divergent executions as ordinary executions or failures without changing admission.

witness.initial: An implementation is admitted after returning a valid output for every trial case, but its output also depends on the sandbox process identifier.
events: An agent submits the implementation and the kernel admits and activates it.
The owner runs the same pinned flow twice with equal inputs in sandbox processes having different identifiers.
outcomes: Both schema-valid outputs are accepted; the implementation remains admitted because the kernel does not check dependence.
The second execution is refused or invalidates the verdict because a function node is promised to be pure and repeatable.
witness.observer: The owner and agent inspecting the two runs and the implementation's admission state.

set_aside.subject: K-02 process facts visible inside the sandbox
set_aside.text: the kernel neither checks that nor masks any other fact of the process
set_aside.question: Which process facts may agent-written code observe, and which must the sandbox hide or normalize to satisfy the separate promises of isolation, no secrets, no service handles and no filesystem beyond the input?
options: Expose all non-secret ambient process facts such as environment entries, process identifiers, locale and platform details
Expose only an explicitly defined sandbox environment and normalize or remove every other ambient fact
Read the phrase literally as exposing every process fact, which conflicts with the rules withholding secrets and service handles
set_aside.default_guess: Expose a minimal explicitly defined non-secret sandbox environment, while treating the existing isolation and secret-withholding rules as overriding the phrase.

witness.initial: The kernel host has a non-secret installation identifier in its environment, while the sandbox specification only says that executions are disposable and isolated.
events: An agent submits a function that reads the ambient environment and returns the installation identifier if present.
outcomes: The trial returns the host identifier because the kernel does not mask process facts.
The environment entry is absent because isolation sanitizes ambient state not declared as function input.
witness.observer: The agent reading the trial evidence.

set_aside.subject: K-02 meaning of output dependence
set_aside.text: code whose outputs depend only on its inputs
set_aside.question: Does the required input-only dependence cover termination, exceptions, timeout and resource behavior as well as returned port values, or only the values produced by successful executions?
options: All observable execution behavior, including success, failure, timeout and resource exhaustion, must depend only on inputs
Only successfully returned port values are covered; nondeterministic failure or timing remains an ordinary execution result
Returned values and success or failure are covered, but trace resource and timing fields are not
set_aside.default_guess: Include success, failure and returned values, but exclude inherently variable trace measurements such as elapsed time and resource usage.

witness.initial: An implementation returns the same valid value whenever it completes, but consults an ambient process fact and sometimes loops until the sandbox timeout.
events: The admission execution completes for a trial case and the implementation is admitted.
A real run invokes the same implementation with the same input and it times out.
outcomes: The timeout is an ordinary bounded execution failure compatible with the promise because no differing output value was returned.
The timeout violates the repeatability condition and the promised continuing verdict because observable termination behavior must also be input-dependent.
witness.observer: The owner or agent inspecting the failed run and relying on the recorded admission verdict.
